```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results=FALSE, output=FALSE}
#Load library so functions run smoothly
library(tidyverse)
```

<center>
![](images/dplyr_join.png){style="width:200px"}
</center>

There are various join functions in `dplyr`.
This page will only show the use of `dplyr::inner_join()`.
This function joins 2 `tibbles`/`data.frames` based on a key column.
This allows you to add data from matching rows similar to VLOOKUP in excel.

[Tidyverse reference page](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org//reference/mutate-joins.html)

## Dataset

Before demonstrating various examples we will create a 2 tibbles:

- `acris_records`: Contain records of frogs from Acris species (Cricket frogs).
- `species_info`: Contains IUCN and lineage information on the the 2 frog

We'll use these for joining.

```{r}
#Vectors for tibble
Species <- c("Acris gryllus","Acris blanchardi","Acris blanchardi","Acris crepitans",
                "Acris crepitans","Acris blanchardi","Acris blanchardi",
                "Acris blanchardi","Acris gryllus","Acris gryllus")
length <- c(32,10,14,23,19,11,9,14,32,22)
#Tibble
acris_records <- tibble::tibble(Species, length)
acris_records
```

Acquire IUCN and lineage information from the `amphibian_div_tbl` data from the [mgrtibbles package](/datasets/mgrtibbles.qmd).

```{r}
#Load package
library("mgrtibbles")
species_info <- mgrtibbles::amphibian_div_tbl |>
    #Select columns
    dplyr::select(Species:Genus) |>
    #Extract distinct/unique rows
    dplyr::distinct() |>
    #Select Acris rows
    dplyr::filter(Genus=="Acris")
species_info
```

## inner_join()

Join 2 `tibbles`/`data.frames` with a key column.
This key column must have the same name and matching values.

```{r}
dplyr::inner_join(
    #Left tibble
    acris_records,
    #Right tibble
    species_info,
    #Key column
    by = "Species"
)
```

Swapping the left and right `tibbles` swaps their positions in the joined `tibble`.

```{r}
dplyr::inner_join(
    #Left tibble
    species_info,
    #Right tibble
    acris_records,
    #Key column
    by = "Species"
)
```
